safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures lip swelling (and dyspnea) but does not include the Gold timeframe of 'past 1 hour.'
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the “past 1 hour” timeframe reduces clarity on acuity and symptom progression, which can matter for triage and handoff in suspected allergic reactions. In this case, the encounter already escalated to emergency action, so the main impact is loss of clinical detail rather than likely change in immediate care.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not specify ~30-minute delay nor localization to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: The ~30-minute post-ingestion onset and upper-lip localization help characterize an IgE-mediated reaction and may assist downstream clinicians in confirming trigger and assessing reaction pattern. Omission mainly affects diagnostic specificity and handoff quality rather than immediate safety in this call.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No documentation in Generated of throat closing sensation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A sensation of throat closing is a key red-flag feature of possible anaphylaxis/upper-airway involvement; missing it in documentation could lead to underestimation of severity by subsequent clinicians. This could adversely affect urgency and treatment decisions if relied upon for handoff or ED triage.

Dizziness can indicate systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension/vasovagal) in an allergic reaction and contributes to anaphylaxis assessment. Its omission may slightly reduce recognition of reaction severity, though it is less critical than airway symptoms.
